slides.title:
A carpenter in Billund,
Denmark, makes *wooden
toys* in the Depression.
slides.sub:
Ole Kirk Kristiansen: yo-yos, cars, planes.
His motto: "Only the best is good enough."

slides.title:
His factory
*burns down*.
He rebuilds it.
slides.sub: It took about a year, in Billund.

slides.title:
The modern *LEGO brick*
is born. A Danish patent
follows the same year.
slides.sub:
The first plastic bricks were sold in 1949.
The 1958 design still clicks today.

slides.title:
Theme parks, more and
more new pieces… LEGO
drifts from *the brick*.
slides.sub:
Sales fall from 1992 to 2004.
"Don't bother us with financial goals"
was the old attitude, says CEO
Jørgen Vig Knudstorp (Fortune, 2006).

slides.title:
employees. Parks *sold*.
Fewer pieces.
Back to the brick.
slides.sub:
The theme parks went for nearly $500M.
They even cut versions of a little chef
minifigure (Fortune, 2006).

slides.title: Our vision is to be based on the LEGO brick — that's our *heritage* and our future.
